subject.title: Browser-heavy sessions block all main lanes — need dedicated browser lane or per-channel lane routing

question: Should OpenClaw solve browser-heavy channel starvation with browser/workload/per-channel lane routing, by folding it into broader per-agent lane policy, or by a different scheduler fairness policy?
rationale: The implementation primitives exist, but exposing lane routing creates public config and fairness guarantees across channels, browser tools, agents, and upgrades.

options.title: Design unified opt-in lane policy
options.body: Keep shared `main` as the default, add maintainer-approved workload/channel/agent lane routing with aggregate caps, and require docs plus regression coverage.

options.title: Fold into per-agent lanes
options.body: Treat this as a browser-heavy use case under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43235 and defer browser/per-channel routing until per-agent isolation proves insufficient.

options.title: Use fairness without new lane config
options.body: Avoid a new lane config surface for now and instead pursue foreground reserves, priority aging, or preemption so fast user turns stay responsive on shared lanes.

recommendation.title: Design unified opt-in lane policy
recommendation.body: Keep shared `main` as the default, add maintainer-approved workload/channel/agent lane routing with aggregate caps, and require docs plus regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal runs through the queue, lane enum, and concurrency-resolution work that define this scheduler contract.
